categories.name: Wrong item/variant selection
categories.definition: The agent selected the wrong product, variant, or replacement item (e.g., wrong color, size, storage capacity, piece count, price-tier, or identical instead of a different variant) instead of identifying and using the correct available item the user wanted or policy required.
categories.boundary: Covers picking the wrong specific item/variant (including exchanging for the identical item or the wrong available option); distinct from wrong action type, wrong order/address target, wrong search criteria, or incomplete data reading.

categories.name: Task type misclassification
categories.definition: The agent treated a request as the wrong action type (e.g., treating a delivered-order return as a cancellation, a tablet swap as a whole-order cancellation, or an exchange as a return) and therefore used the wrong tool or flow for the task.
categories.boundary: Distinct from wrong item selection in that the failure is at the level of which action/tool to apply, not which specific item to select.

categories.name: Wrong order/address identification
categories.definition: The agent confused which order, address, or account data was the old vs. new target (e.g., mixing up which order was older/newer or which to cancel vs. modify) and thus applied changes to the wrong order/address or wrongly claimed the needed data did not exist.
categories.boundary: Covers misidentifying the target entity (order/address) or its old/new semantics even when the action type and item are correct; distinct from wrongly inferring intent, applying wrong policy, or incomplete data reading.

categories.name: Step/turn budget exhaustion
categories.definition: The agent ran out of its step or turn budget (max_steps) before executing required tool calls because it spent turns on redundant/sequential tool calls, excessive clarification, verbose explanation, re-confirmation, or unrelated actions instead of batching or proceeding once confirmation/details were obtained.
categories.boundary: Covers failures caused by resource depletion (including illegal multi-tool calls, one-tool-at-a-time policies, and redundant re-listing) even when the target/data was known but never executed; distinct from execution omission where the agent simply stopped without running out of steps.

categories.name: Execution omission after confirmation
categories.definition: The agent gathered confirmation or identified the needed action but never actually executed the corresponding tool call(s), leaving confirmed tasks unprocessed or transferring away without completing them even though budget remained.
categories.boundary: Distinct from budget exhaustion in that the agent stopped, re-asked, or transferred without executing rather than running out of steps; the correct action and target were already known.

categories.name: Policy/tool misapplication
categories.definition: The agent misread or misapplied a policy or tool contract (e.g., refund destination, cancellation reason, return-vs-exchange rule, address-change dependency, ordering dependency, or a fixed required reason/value) rather than correctly applying the rules or computing the required value.
categories.boundary: Covers misusing the policy/tool itself, recording a wrong mandated value, or inventing a false blocker from policy; distinct from wrong item/order selection, false refusal, and from substituting the user's actual reason without policy mandate.

categories.name: False refusal of valid request
categories.definition: The agent wrongly told the user a valid request could not be done, forced a narrower choice, or refused an individual target action when the request was valid and executable within available tools.
categories.boundary: Covers incorrectly denying/restricting a legitimate request or asserting nonexistence; distinct from policy misapplication in that the agent declines rather than applying a wrong rule, and distinct from scope omission in that it explicitly refuses a single target rather than silently leaving one out.

categories.name: Wrong address-intent inference
categories.definition: The agent reversed or misjudged which address represented the user's old vs. new home and applied address changes in the wrong direction, or allowed a revert that violated the task's required end state, even when both addresses were present in accessible data.
categories.boundary: A specific subtype of target identification focused on old-vs-new address semantics or final default address; distinct from failing to look up available address data.

categories.name: Incomplete data reading
categories.definition: The agent stopped reading a product/order result before reaching the full (often truncated) list or did not fully parse all variant options, and therefore missed an available variant/record, concluded incorrectly that it did not exist, or selected/returned the wrong subset of items.
categories.boundary: Covers premature termination or incomplete parsing of inspected data (including truncated order listings that omit items); distinct from searching with wrong criteria and from selecting the wrong item it did fully see.

categories.name: Wrong search criteria / prioritization
categories.definition: The agent searched, filtered, or prioritized using incorrect criteria (e.g., wrong color, wrong category, deprioritizing a stated preference) and therefore failed to surface or pick the item matching the user's stated preference.
categories.boundary: Distinct from incomplete data reading in that the agent performed a search/ranking with wrong filters or preference weights, rather than truncating an available result set.

categories.name: Wrong payment method / identifier selection
categories.definition: The agent supplied a wrong or fabricated identifier, especially a wrong payment method, card, or other reference, rather than using the actual value available in the data or specified by the user/policy.
categories.boundary: Covers inventing invalid references and selecting a wrong-but-real card/payment value (e.g., using a different stored card than the one instructed); distinct from wrong item/order selection because the wrong entity is an identifier/payment method, not a product or order/address.

categories.name: Scope omission (missed targets)
categories.definition: The agent failed to include one or more of the requested targets in its action scope (e.g., omitting a second order, a second laptop, a bicycle or camera exchange, or not returning all items of an order) even though the user's request or policy required applying the action across all of them.
categories.boundary: Covers leaving out a valid target that was part of a multi-target request or under-returning items on an order; distinct from wrong target identification (acting on the wrong entity) and from false refusal (explicitly denying a single valid request).
